# iru_blueprint_routing (Resource)

Manages the tenant's Blueprint Routing enrollment code, used for Manual and Android Work Profile enrollment.

There is one routing setting per tenant and it always exists, so this resource **cannot create it**: import it with the ID `blueprint_routing`. **Destroy only removes it from Terraform state**; the setting in Iru is left as it is. Routing rules are not exposed by the Iru API and are managed in the Iru UI.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The routing setting always exists: import it (see Import below), then manage
# its enrollment code.
resource "iru_blueprint_routing" "this" {
  enrollment_code = {
    is_active = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `enrollment_code` (Attributes) Routing enrollment code. Attributes left out keep their current value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--enrollment_code))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `blueprint_routing`.

<a id="nestedatt--enrollment_code"></a>
### Nested Schema for `enrollment_code`

Optional:

- `code` (String) The enrollment code.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether the enrollment code is active.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = iru_blueprint_routing.this
  identity = {
    id = "blueprint_routing"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the object in Iru.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = iru_blueprint_routing.this
  id = "blueprint_routing"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# There is one routing setting per tenant; its ID is always blueprint_routing.
# Destroy only removes it from state.
terraform import iru_blueprint_routing.this blueprint_routing
```
